motivation: The separately frozen direct pilot met its signal criterion on a fresh holdout: B T1 AUC 1.0, 16/16 matched pairs in the development-selected direction, no B cross-salt cache hits. This follow-up tests whether the existing BOS W4 changes B's observability or only response ranks.
reuse: Same victim/B document prompts, distinct fresh random 256-bit A/B salts, A warm/cold preparation, 250 ms pause, A target at +15 ms, four B requests at +0/+10/+20/+30 ms, Qwen C0 backend, and unchanged BOS proxy. A target always direct to backend; B's four answers are released as one BOS W4 block.
sessions: Two new engine starts: BOS development 8 matched warm/cold pairs plus 2 A-absent controls; BOS holdout 16 new matched pairs plus 4 controls. Reuse direct-case plan seeds 202611032601 and 202611032602 for matched order/condition schedule, but all salts, engines and responses are new. Train only on BOS development, test BOS holdout.
observers: Same client-only R1/R2/T1/T2/RT definitions and fixed StandardScaler plus LogisticRegression(C=1), with binary T1 AUC direction selected only from BOS development. No direct-session model is reused to avoid a timing-transfer confound. Backend/proxy/cache fields for integrity and measured BOS wait only.
primary: Compare BOS versus direct holdout T1 AUC and T2 accuracy descriptively with uncertainty, as well as R1/R2 response-order signal, full block completion and median/p95 added wait. BOS is not claimed effective merely if one frozen classifier fails; a high T1 AUC means residual information.
decision: If BOS retains T1 AUC at least 0.75 or T2 at least 24/32, with valid cache and full-block integrity, the current release rule does not resolve the observed cross-tenant channel in this local scenario. Recommend a narrowly scoped admission/release design study only then; do not claim a new defense algorithm or broad exploitability from these starts.
limits: Only Qwen C0, one synthetic document family, fixed near-coincident arrival, loopback, no background tenants. Cross-session model comparison is descriptive.
